Business Need: Only authorized admins can add, update or delete products
Observed Finding: TC-05, TC-06 and TC-07 all succeeded with no access token (Auth Needed? = No for every product-changing call)
Recommendation: Require a valid token on add, update and delete and check the admin role; return 401 for a missing or invalid token and 403 for a non-admin user. Treat as a must-have before any real release

Business Need: Invalid or incomplete product data is rejected
Observed Finding: Original TC-12 put {} in the URL and returned 404, so validation was not tested; expected 400 is a BA assumption
Recommendation: If an empty product is accepted, require validation of mandatory fields (such as title and price) and a 400 response naming the missing fields
Next Action: Re-run TC-12 as POST /products/add with body {}

Observed Finding: TC-05 to TC-07 returned success responses but no follow-up GET was done; public demo APIs often simulate writes
Recommendation: If changes are not stored, note the API is suitable for prototyping only and that a real backend must persist data
Next Action: Call GET on the same ID after each add, update and delete and record the result

Business Need: The product list loads quickly and in manageable pages
Observed Finding: List returns 200 with nested product data, but 2,900 ms was the slowest response in the run (above the proposed 2,000 ms target); paging not tested; timings are from a single run
Recommendation: Agree a response-time target with the business, require paging with a sensible default page size, and repeat timings several times
Next Action: Test limit and skip parameters and repeat TC-03 several times

Business Need: Customers can search, filter and sort products
Observed Finding: Not tested; test cases only covered listing all products and fetching one by ID
Recommendation: Check the API documentation for search, category and sort options and add test cases; if missing, raise an enhancement request
Next Action: Add test cases for search, category filter and sorting

Business Need: Customers stay logged in without re-entering their password
Observed Finding: Login returns a refresh token and an invalid or expired access token is rejected with a clear message; the refresh flow itself has not been tested
Recommendation: Test the token refresh request, document how long tokens last, and define what the customer sees when a session expires
Next Action: Test the refresh token request in Postman

Business Need: Clear error messages for failed requests
Observed Finding: Wrong credentials return 400 "Invalid Credentials"; missing and invalid tokens return different 401 messages; a missing product returns 404 with the product ID in the message
Recommendation: No change needed; reuse these messages as the wording standard in requirements and acceptance criteria

Recommendation: No change needed; use the stock field for availability display in the UI requirements (low-stock warnings would be a separate, untested need)
